content.user_title: Refresh AI Focus During Flow Tasks
content.value_statement: Long coding sessions can push original goals out of the model attention. This skill adds refresh checkpoints before key workflow decisions.
actual_capabilities: Defines refresh checkpoints for flow command entry gates.
Guides agents to reread BRAINSTORM.md and TASKS.md before major decisions.
Adds task-start focus checks for flow-dev TDD loops.
Adds Ralph iteration checks using TASKS.md and ERROR_LOG.md.
Defines error recovery refresh steps after test, build, or runtime failures.
Lists red flags that indicate the agent should stop and refresh context.
limitations: Requires planning files such as TASKS.md and BRAINSTORM.md to exist.
Does not execute checks or enforce policy by itself.
Assumes related flow-dev and flow-ralph workflows are present.
Does not validate whether referenced task documents are accurate.

use_cases.title: Keep Long TDD Sessions Aligned
use_cases.description: Use refresh checkpoints before each task so the agent restates the current goal and acceptance criteria.

use_cases.title: Standardize Flow Command Entry Checks
use_cases.description: Apply the same document reread step whenever a flow command starts or changes direction.

use_cases.title: Improve Automated Error Recovery
use_cases.description: Reread recent error notes and the active task before choosing a fix after a failure.

prompt_templates.title: Refresh Before Starting
prompt_templates.prompt: Use flow-attention-refresh before this task. Read the current TASKS.md task and DoD, then summarize the acceptance criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Recover After Failure
prompt_templates.prompt: A test or build failed. Use the error recovery protocol, review ERROR_LOG.md and the active task, then propose the next fix.

prompt_templates.title: Run Ralph Iteration
prompt_templates.prompt: Start the next Ralph iteration. Refresh from the first unfinished TASKS.md item and recent ERROR_LOG.md entries before acting.

prompt_templates.title: Design Refresh Gates
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply this skill to a new flow command. Define when to reread goal files and what each checkpoint must focus on.

output_examples.input: Start the next task after a long conversation.
output_examples.output: The assistant rereads the current task, restates the goal, names the acceptance criteria, and begins only after confirming alignment.

output_examples.input: A build failed during a TDD loop.
output_examples.output: The assistant records the failure, reviews related error history, rereads the task definition, and selects a focused recovery step.
The assistant finds the next unfinished task, checks recent errors, states the immediate action, and avoids repeated mistakes.

best_practices: Keep TASKS.md, BRAINSTORM.md, quickstart.md, and ERROR_LOG.md current.
Use a refresh checkpoint before each major decision or task transition.
Ask the agent to restate acceptance criteria before implementation starts.
anti_patterns: Starting a task from memory after many tool calls.
Fixing failures without reading recent error history.
Using the protocol when project planning files are missing or stale.

faq.question: What problem does this skill solve?
faq.answer: It helps an AI agent regain focus on the original goal during long development sessions.

faq.question: Does it run commands?
faq.answer: No. It is a Markdown protocol that tells the agent which project documents to reread.

faq.question: Which files does it expect?
faq.answer: It references BRAINSTORM.md, TASKS.md, quickstart.md, and ERROR_LOG.md when those files are relevant.

faq.question: Can it work outside the flow workflow?
faq.answer: Yes, but it is most useful when similar planning and error log files exist.

faq.question: Is this a security tool?
faq.answer: No. It is a workflow focus aid for AI-assisted coding tasks.

faq.question: Why were command findings dismissed?
faq.answer: The flagged backticks are Markdown formatting and examples, not executable command calls.
